Tier 2 (a wait with no bound and no error, hand drivers only). Found by the claims verifier of round 9 of PR #1253's per-PR verification (lever phase before pass 12, #1226) and confirmed by an independent verifier; a regression of that PR against its base, carried into pass 12 by the user's decision (the PR's verification was capped at round 9, and landing the Tier 1 fix with this documented limit was judged the safer tree).

**What:** `pgpm._snapshot_wait` (PR #1253, `pgpm_core/install.sql` about line 7576 on its head `6f05d177`) breaks a cycle of waits only when the YOUNGEST wait lists an older wait's marker. A cycle closed through a third session that the older wait PASSES has no such edge. Concretely, all three by hand under `lock_timeout` 0 (the session default the reference names for hand calls):

- A, a hand `pgpm.regrain()` on parent `rga`, the OLDER wait (its reference is its own xid), holds SHARE on `rga`.
- C, a REPEATABLE READ session whose snapshot predates `rgb`'s copies and whose next statement, an INSERT into `rga`, queues behind A's SHARE lock. A passes C with its WARNING (the own-xid direct pass: C is directly blocked by A's own lock).
- B, a hand `pgpm.regrain_step` at `rgb`'s swap, the YOUNGER wait, against the run's recorded last write (`regrain_written_xid`). B lists C (C's xmin is at or before that write) and waits for it. B does NOT list A, whose xmin is past that write, so B never sees A's marker and never yields.
- A lists B (B's xmin is at or before A's xid) and, being older, never yields.

So A waits for B, B waits for C, C waits on A's lock; none of the three rules (chain, peer, direct) fires; A and B poll in `pg_sleep` with `pg_blocking_pids` empty, A holding SHARE on `rga` so every write to it queues, with no error, until a `statement_timeout`, if the callers set one. Reproduced twice on the head: 8 s after the gate opened A and B were both in PgSleep with no blocking pids and C was blocked by A; A ended only at its 25 s `statement_timeout`, after which B swapped. The base (no wait) completes both calls at once.

**Reach:** both A and B must be hand calls under `lock_timeout` 0. With `maintain` in B's place its 200 ms budget defers B and the cycle ends; `from_hypertable_cutover` breaks it at its `p_lock_timeout`. A `statement_timeout` on either hand call bounds it.

**What the PR does about it:** documents the limit in `docs/reference.md` (hand `regrain()` and `regrain_step` run together can wait on each other through a session one of them passes; set a `statement_timeout` or `lock_timeout` on hand calls) in place of the earlier "in any cycle of waits the youngest lists an older one" claim. The fix proper is a generalisation of the peer rule: a waiter also yields to an older marker holder that a session it lists is lock-blocked by, directly or through a chain (the `pg_blocking_pids` closure the chain rule already computes), so a cycle through a passed session has the yielding edge. Acceptance: the verifier's reproduction (`lever12/pv/1253_r9/pr/claims/V/V-01/repro.sh`: A, B and C as above from dblink and direct sessions, LIVENESS that the three-way dependency holds, defect checks that the younger yields within seconds and A swaps), tests/328's part shape (R, S, T), a mutation that drops the new edge.
title: pgpm._snapshot_wait: a cycle of two hand waits closed through a REPEATABLE READ session the older wait passes is never broken (hand regrain() and regrain_step under lock_timeout 0 wait until a statement_timeout, SHARE held on one parent)

Tier 3 (a contract not kept: the #272 bar, "a reconcile tick's work scales with its budget, not with the delta"). Found by the residue verification of the lever phase before pass 12 (#1226): fixer X8 of PR #1253 reported that `bench/regrain_perf.sh` fails on correct code in a plain `pgpm_test:15` container; one verifier (R2) against `main` at `e6f73bf3` found the guard is right to fail, and that the cause is in pgpm, not the harness.

**What:** on PostgreSQL 15 a regrain reconcile tick reads the whole capture delta by sequential scan, twice. The tick's batch predicate, `k.pgpm_seq = any($1) and k.ctid = any($2)` with a 3000-element array (`pgpm_core/install.sql` about line 6282 on `e6f73bf3`), is planned as a Seq Scan on the delta table by PG 15's planner, both in the distinct-sub-range select (about line 6285) and in the batch delete (about line 6401). The verifier's reproduction reads 100001 rows for a 3000-row batch of a 50000-row delta on PG 15.19 (`auto_explain` shows the Seq Scan in the batch statement's own plan), and 1 row (the exists probe) on PG 17.11; a 500-element array plans the `pgpm_seq` index on PG 15, so the boundary is the planner's ScalarArrayOp costing, which PG 17 changed. Draining a large delta on 15 is therefore O(delta^2 / batch), the regression #272 fixed.

**Why nothing guards it:** `bench/regrain_perf.sh`, the guard of that bar, only runs on PG 17 (`./test.sh perf` and CI's perf job both use `pgpm_test-17`), where the planner picks the index. The pass-7 Mac observation recorded on #871 ("100001 > 12500 on plain pgpm_test:15") is this mechanism, not the counter flush #871 is about; #871 stays open for its own CI direction (the counter read 0 on PG 17). The defect pre-dates #1070: the tree before `2a7715a7` reads the same 100001 on PG 15. Not a statistics artefact: the guard's own read (a fresh backend after `pg_stat_force_next_flush`) equals a settled read taken 2 s later after `pg_stat_clear_snapshot`, and autovacuum and autoanalyze never touched the delta. PG 16 was not run (no private container); PG 18 was reported passing by the fixer.

**Remedy:** two parts, both needed. (1) The guard must run where the planner differs: `bench/regrain_perf.sh` on PG 15 as well as 17 (the perf track's matrix, or a second invocation), or the bar is unmeasured on a supported version. (2) A predicate every supported planner indexes: for instance a range on `pgpm_seq` when a batch is contiguous by sequence (`pgpm_seq between lo and hi`), or an `unnest` join that plans a nested-loop index scan, in place of the 3000-element `= any($1)`; measure the fix with the same guard on 15 and 17.

**Reproduction:** `R2-01/repro.sh` in the phase's scratch (`lever12/residue/claims/R2/R2-01/`): the guard's own fixture (a 100000-row table transmuted with a two-thirds frontier, six ticks, a 25000-row update captured into a delta of at least 40000 rows, LIVENESS-checked), then one tick's `seq_tup_read` delta on the capture table read from a fresh backend; fails when the tick reads more than a quarter of the delta, passes when it reads one batch. Fails on `e6f73bf3` in `pgpm_prv-15`, passes on PG 17.
title: regrain reconcile tick seq-scans the whole capture delta on PostgreSQL 15 (a 3000-element = any($1) batch predicate plans as a Seq Scan): the #272 bar unguarded because bench/regrain_perf.sh runs only on PG 17

  && echo "ok - LIVENESS: the fixture registered public.messages" || { echo "not ok - LIVENESS: the fixture registered public.messages"; exit 1; }
for f in 02_routing_test.sql 06_obtain_test.sql 08_index_propagation_test.sql; do

  # each run inside a transaction that is rolled back, so the two runs see the same fixture

  if grep -q "not ok" <<<"$base" || ! grep -qE '^ok [0-9]' <<<"$base"; then
    echo "not ok - LIVENESS: tests/$f passes in the month the template was built"; exit 1; fi

  shifted=$( { echo "begin;"; sed "s/now()/(now() + interval '1 month')/g" "$T"; echo "rollback;"; } | $PSQL -tA 2>&1)

    echo "not ok - tests/$f fails when it runs in the month after the template's: $(grep -m2 'not ok' <<<"$shifted" | tr '\n' ' ')"; fail=1

- finder: B04

- tier: 4

The table is still a hypertable; transmute refuses it (inheritance children) and transmute_abort has nothing to abort. - root cause (verifier): _from_hypertable_check_arguments (pgpm_hypertable:440) passes _time_unit_contract's transmute-only remedy text through unwrapped, so a pre-copy hypertable refusal tells the operator to re-run transmute and transmute_abort instead of from_hypertable

Reproduction: `repro.sh`, the finder's, run unchanged by the verifier.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# B04-03: from_hypertable asks transmute's column-unit rules (pgpm._time_unit_contract) of the hypertable before
# its copy (#1118, #1138 bullet 2, PR #1212), and the refusal is transmute's own text, whose remedy is "then
# re-run transmute; if an earlier attempt left a pgpm_monolith_bound CHECK on the table, call
# pgpm.transmute_abort(<table>) first". Raised from from_hypertable with the hypertable untouched, that sends the
# operator to transmute, which refuses a hypertable (inheritance children), and to transmute_abort, which has
# nothing to abort: the call to re-run is from_hypertable. Two sites: the date-anchor message (#769) and the
# timestamp(p) message (#1039). Defect present: the refusal names transmute as the re-run. Absent: it names
# from_hypertable (or says nothing of transmute).
set -u
fail=0
q() { $PSQL -tAc "$1" 2>&1; }
q "set client_min_messages=warning; create table public.b4t (ts timestamptz(0) not null, v int)" >/dev/null
q "set client_min_messages=warning; select create_hypertable('public.b4t','ts', chunk_time_interval=>interval '1 day')" >/dev/null
q "insert into public.b4t select now() - g*interval '1 hour', g from generate_series(1,10) g" >/dev/null
q "set client_min_messages=warning; create table public.b4d (d date not null, v int)" >/dev/null
q "set client_min_messages=warning; select create_hypertable('public.b4d','d', chunk_time_interval=>interval '7 days')" >/dev/null
q "insert into public.b4d select current_date - g, 100 + g from generate_series(1,10) g" >/dev/null
n=$(q "select count(*) from timescaledb_information.hypertables where hypertable_schema='public' and hypertable_name in ('b4t','b4d')")
if [ "$n" = "2" ]; then echo "ok 1 - GUARD: fixture: b4t (timestamptz(0)) and b4d (date) are hypertables"; else echo "not ok 1 - GUARD: fixture: two hypertables (got $n)"; fail=1; fi

out_t=$(q "call pgpm.from_hypertable('public.b4t','ts', interval '500 milliseconds')")
out_d=$(q "call pgpm.from_hypertable('public.b4d','d', interval '1 day', p_anchor => '2000-01-01 12:00:00+00')")
if echo "$out_t" | grep -q "keeps whole seconds only"; then echo "ok 2 - LIVENESS: from_hypertable refused the sub-second step on the timestamptz(0) dimension by the #1039 unit rule"; else echo "not ok 2 - LIVENESS: timestamp(p) refusal (got: $(echo "$out_t" | head -c 300))"; fail=1; fi
if echo "$out_d" | grep -q "must fall at 00:00 UTC"; then echo "ok 3 - LIVENESS: from_hypertable refused the noon anchor on the date dimension by the #769 rule"; else echo "not ok 3 - LIVENESS: date-anchor refusal (got: $(echo "$out_d" | head -c 300))"; fail=1; fi
n=$(q "select count(*) from timescaledb_information.hypertables where hypertable_schema='public' and hypertable_name in ('b4t','b4d')")
if [ "$n" = "2" ]; then echo "ok 4 - LIVENESS: both refusals came before the copy and the swap: both tables are still hypertables"; else echo "not ok 4 - LIVENESS: both still hypertables (got $n)"; fail=1; fi
# what the named remedy does when followed: transmute on the hypertable, with a step the rule accepts
rem=$(q "call pgpm.transmute('public.b4t','ts', interval '1 second')")
if echo "$rem" | grep -q "inheritance children"; then echo "ok 5 - LIVENESS: following the remedy as written (re-run transmute, corrected step) is refused: transmute cannot take a hypertable"; else echo "not ok 5 - LIVENESS: transmute on the hypertable refused (got: $(echo "$rem" | head -c 300))"; fail=1; fi

for pair in "t:$out_t" "d:$out_d"; do
  k=${pair%%:*}; msg=${pair#*:}
  if echo "$msg" | grep -q "re-run transmute\|transmute_abort("; then
    echo "not ok - the $k refusal raised by from_hypertable sends the operator to transmute / transmute_abort (the re-run is from_hypertable): $(echo "$msg" | grep -o 'then re-run transmute[^.]*' | head -1)"; fail=1
  else
    echo "ok - the $k refusal raised by from_hypertable does not name transmute as the re-run"
  fi
done
exit $fail
```

Tier 4. Found by the pass-11 fix phase's per-PR verification of PR #1195 and verified there; pre-existing on main. Related: #1117, #814.

**Where:** `pgpm_core/install.sql:6890`

**Scenario:** warn_grid_off_unit is documented as logged once per grid (reference log table; the block's comment 'a re-run of this file finds the row and does not repeat it'), but the dedup key is the rendered message, which embeds parent_table::text as the upgrading session's search_path renders it, so the same off-unit grid app.g1 flagged by an upgrade under the default search_path ('app.g1') is logged a second time by an upgrade under 'app, public' ('g1'); it should be logged once per grid whatever the session's search_path (dedup on parent and action, or render the name schema-qualified)

**Root cause (verifier):** warn_grid_off_unit's once-per-grid dedup (pgpm_core/install.sql:6889-6891, head) keys on the rendered message (l.method = v_msg_q), which embeds cfg.parent_table::text (search_path-relative) and _reconvert_remedy's rendering, so an upgrade under another search_path logs the same grid again (rerun: 2 rows, 'app.g1' then 'g1'); the same text also renders partition_anchor (%s, session TimeZone) and partition_step (IntervalStyle), so each distinct session rendering adds one row. docs/reference.md:3383 says 'Logged once per grid' and the block's comment says 'a re-run of this file finds the row and does not repeat it'. Consequence bounded to one extra log row per distinct rendering (no code reads these rows; the WARNING is documented as raised on every run), so Tier 4 by the rubric, not 3. NOT pre-existing in substance: the base tree has no warn_grid_off_unit block at all (the base run fails on its LIVENESS checks, 0 rows), so this is introduced by PR #1195 and the 'pre_existing' class is an artifact of the liveness failure on base. Same class as #814 (session settings leaking into compared text) but a new site #814 cannot name; not known_open. Original repro kept unchanged (it reaches the defect on head on its own; no base rebuild is possible since the unit does not exist there).

**Reproduction** (`repro.sh`; fails while the defect is present, passes when absent; install: pgpm_core/install.sql):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The upgrade's warn_grid_off_unit is documented as "Logged once per grid" (docs/reference.md's log table; the
# block's comment: "logged once (a re-run of this file finds the row and does not repeat it)"). The dedup key
# is the rendered message text (l.method = v_msg_q), and the message embeds cfg.parent_table::text twice
# (the subject and _reconvert_remedy's %L), which regclass output renders relative to the SESSION's
# search_path. So the same grid, re-flagged by an upgrade run under another search_path (a table in schema
# app: 'app.g1' under the default path, 'g1' under 'app, public'), is logged a second time. Expected: one
# warn_grid_off_unit row for the grid however many upgrades run, whatever their search_path.
set -u
set -o pipefail
fail=0
say() { echo "$1"; case "$1" in "not ok"*) fail=1;; esac; }
q() { $PSQL -X -q -tA -c "set timezone='UTC'" -c "set client_min_messages=warning" -c "$1" 2>&1; }

$PSQL -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f - >/dev/null 2>&1 <<'SQL'
set timezone = 'UTC';
set client_min_messages = warning;
create schema app;
create table app.g1 (id bigint, dt date not null, primary key (id, dt));
insert into app.g1 select g, date '2024-08-01' + (g % 60) from generate_series(1, 20) g;
call pgpm.transmute('app.g1', 'dt', interval '1 month', p_obtain => 1);
-- an older install's registration: a date grid anchored at noon (tests/324's d324)
update pgpm.config set partition_anchor = '2000-01-01 12:00:00+00' where parent_table = 'app.g1'::regclass;
SQL
[ $? = 0 ] && say "ok - fixture: app.g1 converted and its noon anchor planted" \
           || { say "not ok - fixture: app.g1 converted and its noon anchor planted"; exit 1; }

# upgrade 1: the default search_path ("$user", public), so the table renders as app.g1
out1=$($PSQL -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction -f - < "$TREE/pgpm_core/install.sql" 2>&1)
[ $? = 0 ] && say "ok - fixture: upgrade 1 (default search_path) ran" || { say "not ok - fixture: upgrade 1 ran"; exit 1; }
r=$(q "select count(*) from pgpm.log where action = 'warn_grid_off_unit' and parent_table = 'app.g1'::regclass")
[ "$r" = 1 ] && say "ok - LIVENESS: upgrade 1 flagged app.g1 once" || say "not ok - LIVENESS: upgrade 1 flagged app.g1 once ($r)"

# upgrade 2: the same file, the same grid, run by a session whose search_path includes app
out2=$( { echo "set search_path = app, public;"; cat "$TREE/pgpm_core/install.sql"; } \
        | $PSQL -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction -f - 2>&1)
[ $? = 0 ] && say "ok - fixture: upgrade 2 (search_path app, public) ran" || { say "not ok - fixture: upgrade 2 ran"; echo "$out2" | tail -3; exit 1; }
case "$out2" in *"WARNING:"*"grid of g1 is off"*) say "ok - LIVENESS: upgrade 2 found the same grid off its unit and raised its WARNING";;
  *) say "not ok - LIVENESS: upgrade 2 found the same grid off its unit and raised its WARNING";; esac

r=$(q "select string_agg(method, ' || ' order by id) from pgpm.log where action = 'warn_grid_off_unit' and parent_table = 'app.g1'::regclass")
n=$(q "select count(*) from pgpm.log where action = 'warn_grid_off_unit' and parent_table = 'app.g1'::regclass")
echo "# rows: ${r:0:400}"
[ "$n" = 1 ] && say "ok - app.g1 is logged once across the two upgrades" \
             || say "not ok - app.g1 is logged once across the two upgrades ($n rows, one per rendering of its name)"
exit $fail
```

Tier 3. Found by the pass-11 fix phase's per-PR verification of PR #1212 and verified there; pre-existing on main. Related: #1118, #1138, #1105.

**Where:** `pgpm_hypertable/install.sql:2375`

**Scenario:** Sibling of #1118 left by PR #1212: transmute's session-zone rule (#455, _canonical_tz: a timestamptz grid records the session TimeZone and refuses one not in pg_timezone_names, e.g. 'UTC+3' or 'localtime') is asked of from_hypertable only by the handoff transmute, after the cutover's swap committed and dropped the hypertable; a timestamptz hypertable migrated from such a session is left a plain table pgpm does not manage (rows intact). _from_hypertable_check_arguments asks the column-type grid rules now, not this one.

**Root cause (verifier):** from_hypertable never asks transmute's #455 session-zone rule (pgpm._canonical_tz(current_setting('TimeZone')), pgpm_core/install.sql:9074) before its copy: _from_hypertable_check_arguments (pgpm_hypertable/install.sql ~430) asks only _refuse_bad_transmute_arguments and _time_unit_contract, so a timestamptz hypertable migrated from a session under 'UTC+3' (or localtime/posixrules/Factory) runs the copy, commits the swap that drops the hypertable, and is refused only at the handoff, leaving a plain unmanaged table (rows intact). Reproduced unchanged on base and head (pre_existing; 0:37:0 after the call). Not intended: reference.md:760-765 lists from_hypertable's before-the-copy refusals and omits the zone, and the 'handoff can still refuse' paragraph (reference.md:1019) covers transmute's preconditions on the table's state, not a session setting (the reading #1118's verifier gave). Not known-open: #1118 is the #581 date-step rule and #1138 b2 the #769 date-anchor rule (both the column-type rules this PR now asks); #816 b3 names only #710 and #766; #1111 is a stored 'localtime' surviving an upgrade. Tier 3, not worse: continuous aggregates are refused up front (pgpm_hypertable ~775), every row reaches the plain table, and the documented remedy (set a named zone, then transmute + restore/validate_incoming_fks) finishes the handoff; it acts (drops the hypertable, pays the copy) where it should refuse. The rule is a session rule, so it belongs in the same up-front argument contract the PR extends, asked by from_hypertable before its copy and by the cutover before its pre-drain.

**Reproduction** (`repro.sh`; fails while the defect is present, passes when absent; install: pgpm_core/install.sql, pgpm_hypertable/install.sql, tests/timescale/fixtures.sql):

```bash

# V-01: a sibling of #1118 on the same surface. transmute records the transmuting session's TimeZone as a
# timestamptz grid's zone and refuses a session zone it cannot record (_canonical_tz: not a pg_timezone_names
# name, e.g. a POSIX rule such as 'UTC+3', or 'localtime'), "checked before anything is committed, so a refusal
# costs nothing" (pgpm_core/install.sql, #455). from_hypertable never asks it up front, so on a timestamptz
# hypertable the copy runs, the cutover's swap commits and drops the hypertable, and only the handoff transmute
# refuses: a plain table pgpm does not manage (rows intact).
# Defect present: after the refused call ts_t is no longer a hypertable. Absent: refused before the copy.
set -u
fail=0
$PSQL -tAc "create extension if not exists timescaledb" >/dev/null 2>&1
$PSQL -tAc "set client_min_messages=warning; create table public.ts_t(ts timestamptz not null, v int not null)" >/dev/null
$PSQL -tAc "set client_min_messages=warning; select create_hypertable('public.ts_t','ts', chunk_time_interval=>interval '7 days')" >/dev/null
$PSQL -tAc "insert into public.ts_t select date_trunc('hour', now()) - g * interval '1 hour', g from generate_series(1,37) g" >/dev/null
# the operator's sessions run under a POSIX-rule zone (set for the database, so every session the call opens has it)
$PSQL -tAc "do \$\$ begin execute format('alter database %I set timezone = %L', current_database(), 'UTC+3'); end \$\$" >/dev/null
tz=$($PSQL -tAc "select current_setting('TimeZone') || ':' || (pgpm._canonical_tz(current_setting('TimeZone')) is null)")
if [ "$tz" = "UTC+3:true" ]; then echo "ok - GUARD: a new session runs under UTC+3, a zone _canonical_tz does not record"; else echo "not ok - GUARD: a new session runs under UTC+3, a zone _canonical_tz does not record (got $tz)"; fail=1; fi
before=$($PSQL -tAc "select (select count(*) from timescaledb_information.hypertables where hypertable_schema='public' and hypertable_name='ts_t') || ':' || (select count(*) from public.ts_t)")
if [ "$before" = "1:37" ]; then echo "ok - LIVENESS: ts_t is a hypertable holding its 37 rows before the call"; else echo "not ok - LIVENESS: ts_t is a hypertable holding its 37 rows before the call (got $before)"; fail=1; fi
out=$($PSQL -tAc "call pgpm.from_hypertable('public.ts_t','ts', interval '1 day')" 2>&1)
if echo "$out" | grep -q "TimeZone (UTC+3) is not a zone pgpm can record"; then echo "ok - LIVENESS: the call was refused on transmute's session-zone rule"; else echo "not ok - LIVENESS: the call was refused on transmute's session-zone rule (got: $(echo "$out" | head -c 300))"; fail=1; fi
after=$($PSQL -tAc "select (select count(*) from timescaledb_information.hypertables where hypertable_schema='public' and hypertable_name='ts_t') || ':' || (select count(*) from public.ts_t) || ':' || (select count(*) from pgpm.config where parent_table::text = 'ts_t')")
if [ "$(echo "$after" | cut -d: -f2)" = "37" ]; then echo "ok - fixture: every row is still in ts_t"; else echo "not ok - fixture: every row is still in ts_t (got $after)"; fi
if [ "$(echo "$after" | cut -d: -f1)" = "1" ]; then echo "ok - the refused call left ts_t a hypertable (refused before the swap)"; else echo "not ok - the refused call dropped the hypertable: ts_t is now a plain table pgpm does not manage (hypertable:rows:managed = $after)"; fail=1; fi
$PSQL -tAc "do \$\$ begin execute format('alter database %I reset timezone', current_database()); end \$\$" >/dev/null
exit $fail
```

**Scenario:** #1162's quadratic survives in maintain_obtain's back-off walk, which the PR leaves asking _cell_attached once per step (the body names it as not covered). A tick that honours an armed back-off (the 30 s after a real deferral: obtain lost the lock race to a session holding ACCESS SHARE on the parent) walks ceil(obtain / 2) + 1 steps, each scanning every attached pgpm.part row through _native_gt: 40,904 _native_gt calls at lookahead 200 against 643,604 at 800 (15.7x for 4x), identical on base and head. Reached by the pgpm_obtain job when p_obtain_every is under 30 s, or by any maintain_obtain call inside a back-off; on the default every-minute cadence a tick rarely lands inside the 30 s window, so the cost is narrower than #1162's (every tick), but it is the same O(lookahead x partitions) shape under sustained contention, which is exactly when back-offs re-arm.

**Root cause (verifier):** maintain_obtain's back-off walk (pgpm_core/install.sql ~12476 on head, unchanged from base) asks _cell_attached once per grid step, and each ask scans every attached pgpm.part row through _native_gt, so a tick honouring an armed back-off does about ceil(obtain/2) x partitions comparisons (re-run: 40,904 at lookahead 200 vs 643,604 at 800, 15.7x for 4x, identical on base and head, all five liveness witnesses passing). A distinct sibling site of #1162's mechanism, not #1162's own bullet: #1162 names only 'obtain's lookahead walk' and 'every run of the every-minute obtain job', never the back-off walk, and the PR (which fixes #1162's one bullet) states in its body 'Not covered: maintain_obtain's back-off walk still asks _cell_attached per step ... left as a follow-up'; no open issue names it, and the PR's own issue does not count as known_open for the residue it leaves. Not documented as intended: the walk's comment says only 'it costs at most ceil(obtain / 2) + 1 grid steps', which bounds steps, not the per-step partition scan. Tier 3 as #1162 is (a cost contract not kept, the tick completes; narrower because it bites only inside the 30 s back-off, i.e. under sustained contention or p_obtain_every under 30 s). The two mutations anchored on the walk's text (obtain_headroom_ignores_monolith, obtain_backoff_counts_hole) are a fix cost (they must be re-anchored with the change), not a reason to call it a lever: it is a one-site fix using the PR's own _cell_walk_rows/_cell_walk_step. Original reproduction used unchanged.

**Reproduction** (`repro.sh`; fails while the defect is present, passes when absent; install: pgpm_core/install.sql):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# V-01 (#1162 sibling): maintain_obtain's back-off walk still asks _cell_attached once per step, and each ask
# scans every attached pgpm.part row of the parent through _native_gt, so a tick that HONOURS an armed
# back-off (the 30 s after a deferral) does about ceil(obtain / 2) x partitions comparisons: quadratic in the
# lookahead, the cost #1162 removed from obtain's own walk. The back-off is armed for real: a second session
# holds ACCESS SHARE on the parent while maintain_obtain's obtain needs a new cell, so obtain loses the lock
# race (lock_timeout 200 ms), logs skip_obtain and arms obtain_retry_after. The next maintain_obtain, inside
# the 30 s, walks the coverage and keeps the back-off. Counted from pg_stat_user_functions (track_functions
# = 'pl', instrumentation only), read in a later transaction than the call, after a forced flush.
set -uo pipefail
fail=0
say() { if [ "$1" = ok ]; then echo "ok - $2"; else echo "not ok - $2"; fail=1; fi; }

measure() {   # $1 table, $2 lookahead; prints "<calls> <status> <deferred> <armed>"
  local t=$1 n=$2
  $PSQL -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 >/dev/null <<SQL
set client_min_messages = warning;
create table public.$t (id bigint primary key, v text);
insert into public.$t values (1, 'a');
call pgpm.transmute('public.$t', 'id', 10::bigint, p_obtain => $n, p_paused => false);
SQL
  # fill the grid to its lookahead (obtain's lock budget can stop a call short), one obtain per transaction
  local i m
  for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do m=$($PSQL -qtAc "select pgpm.obtain('public.$t')"); [ "$m" = 0 ] && break; done
  # the frontier moves up one cell, so obtain needs one new cell at the top of the grid
  $PSQL -qtAc "insert into public.$t values (15, 'b')" >/dev/null
  # the second session: holds ACCESS SHARE on the parent for 4 s
  docker exec "$CONTAINER" psql -U postgres -d "$DB" -qc \
    "begin; lock table public.$t in access share mode; select pg_sleep(4); commit;" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  local bg=$!
  sleep 1
  local s1; s1=$($PSQL -qtAc "call pgpm.maintain_obtain('public.$t')")
  wait $bg
  local deferred; deferred=$($PSQL -qtAc "select count(*) from pgpm.log where parent_table = 'public.$t'::regclass and action = 'skip_obtain'")
  local armed; armed=$($PSQL -qtAc "select obtain_retry_after > clock_timestamp() from pgpm.config where parent_table = 'public.$t'::regclass")
  local out
  out=$($PSQL -qtA <<SQL
set track_functions = 'pl';
select pg_stat_force_next_flush();
select pg_sleep(0.2);
select pg_stat_clear_snapshot();
create temporary table c0 as select coalesce(sum(calls), 0) as c from pg_stat_user_functions where schemaname = 'pgpm' and funcname = '_native_gt';
call pgpm.maintain_obtain('public.$t');
select pg_stat_force_next_flush();
select pg_sleep(0.2);
select pg_stat_clear_snapshot();
select 'R', (select coalesce(sum(calls), 0) from pg_stat_user_functions where schemaname = 'pgpm' and funcname = '_native_gt') - (select c from c0);
SQL
)
  local calls; calls=$(echo "$out" | grep '^R|' | cut -d'|' -f2)
  local s2; s2=$(echo "$out" | grep '^obtained=' | tail -1)
  local built; built=$($PSQL -qtAc "select count(*) from pgpm.part where parent_table = 'public.$t'::regclass and attached")
  echo "$calls|$s2|$deferred|$armed|$s1|$built"
}

A=$(measure v01a 200); B=$(measure v01b 800)
echo "# lookahead 200: $A"; echo "# lookahead 800: $B"
ca=$(echo "$A" | cut -d'|' -f1); cb=$(echo "$B" | cut -d'|' -f1)
sa=$(echo "$A" | cut -d'|' -f2); sb=$(echo "$B" | cut -d'|' -f2)
[ "$(echo "$A" | cut -d'|' -f3)" -ge 1 ] && [ "$(echo "$B" | cut -d'|' -f3)" -ge 1 ] && say ok "LIVENESS: obtain lost the lock race on both tables (skip_obtain logged)" || say no "LIVENESS: obtain lost the lock race on both tables (skip_obtain logged)"
[ "$(echo "$A" | cut -d'|' -f4)" = t ] && [ "$(echo "$B" | cut -d'|' -f4)" = t ] && say ok "LIVENESS: the back-off is armed (obtain_retry_after in the future)" || say no "LIVENESS: the back-off is armed (obtain_retry_after in the future)"
case "$sa$sb" in *bypassed*) say no "LIVENESS: the measured ticks honoured the back-off (walked it, did not bypass): '$sa' '$sb'";;
  *) if [[ "$sa" == *obtain_backoff* && "$sb" == *obtain_backoff* ]]; then say ok "LIVENESS: the measured ticks honoured the back-off (walked it, did not bypass)"; else say no "LIVENESS: the measured ticks honoured the back-off: '$sa' '$sb'"; fi;; esac
na=$(echo "$A" | cut -d'|' -f6); nb=$(echo "$B" | cut -d'|' -f6)
[ "$na" -ge 200 ] && [ "$na" -le 203 ] && [ "$nb" -ge 800 ] && [ "$nb" -le 803 ] && say ok "LIVENESS: the two grids are built to their lookaheads ($na, $nb partitions)" || say no "LIVENESS: the two grids are built to their lookaheads ($na, $nb partitions)"
[[ "$ca" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [ "$ca" -ge 100 ] && say ok "LIVENESS: the function counter sees the walk's comparisons ($ca at lookahead 200)" || say no "LIVENESS: the function counter sees the walk's comparisons ('$ca')"
if [[ "$ca" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$cb" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [ "$ca" -gt 0 ] && [ $((cb * 1)) -lt $((ca * 8)) ]; then
  say ok "a backed-off tick at 4x the lookahead does under 8x the comparisons ($ca vs $cb)"
else
  say no "a backed-off tick at 4x the lookahead does under 8x the comparisons ($ca vs $cb; linear is ~4x, quadratic ~16x)"
fi
exit $fail
```

Tier 3. Found by the pass-11 fix phase's per-PR verification of PR #1198 and verified there; pre-existing on main. Related: #1158.

**Where:** `pgpm_hypertable/install.sql:1559`

**Scenario:** two online append drains of one keyless hypertable at once (an operator's directly driven from_hypertable_drain_appends(_step) beside another, e.g. the cutover's default p_predrain): both read the same copy watermark and insert the same batch, since the ROW EXCLUSIVE every drain now takes on the copy (#1158) does not conflict with itself and no other lock serialises two drains; the copy holds the batch twice and every later cutover refuses on the conservation check until the copy is rebuilt. A drain should wait for, or refuse beside, another drain of the same hypertable.

**Root cause (verifier):** nothing serialises two append drains of one hypertable: from_hypertable_drain_appends reads the copy's watermark under ROW EXCLUSIVE on the copy (#1158), which does not conflict with itself, so a second drain beside one in flight (an operator's directly driven drain, which docs/reference.md permits 'during a long two-phase window', beside another or beside the cutover's default p_predrain) re-reads the stale watermark and inserts the same batch; the keyless copy holds it twice (1,2,3,4,100,100,101,101, reproduced on base and head by my re-run). Tier 3, not 1 or 2: the conservation check (count and fingerprint) refuses every later swap so no duplicate reaches the migrated table and no row is lost, and a documented re-run of from_hypertable_copy rebuilds the copy; but the drain acts where it should wait or refuse, against its own comment's 'no race' and the reference's 'takes turns with the cutover on the copy', and the refusal misattributes the surplus to out-of-order appends. Not #1158 by mechanism (drain vs cutover pre-lock read, which this PR fixes); no open issue names drain vs drain.

**Reproduction** (`repro.sh`; fails while the defect is present, passes when absent; install: pgpm_core/install.sql, pgpm_hypertable/install.sql):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# V-01: two online append drains of one KEYLESS hypertable running at once (an operator's directly driven
# from_hypertable_drain_appends(_step), which the reference says may be driven during a long two-phase window,
# beside another one, e.g. the cutover's own default p_predrain) both read the same copy watermark and both
# insert the same batch. #1158's fix gives every drain ROW EXCLUSIVE on the copy, which does not conflict with
# itself, so nothing serialises two drains: the copy ends up holding the batch twice, and every later cutover
# refuses on the conservation check until the whole copy is rebuilt.
# Deterministic: drain A's step runs in an open transaction (batch uncommitted) while drain B (the procedure)
# reads the watermark, which cannot see A's rows yet, and drains the same rows; then A commits.
set -u
fail=0
q() { $PSQL -X -q -tA -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@"; }

q -c "create extension if not exists timescaledb" \
  -c "create schema v01" \
  -c "create table v01.e (ts timestamptz not null, v int not null)" \
  -c "select create_hypertable('v01.e', 'ts', chunk_time_interval => interval '1 day', create_default_indexes => false)" \
  -c "insert into v01.e select now() - g * interval '5 hours', g from generate_series(1, 4) g" \
  -c "call pgpm.from_hypertable_copy('v01.e', 'ts')" \
  -c "insert into v01.e values (now() - interval '30 minutes', 100), (now() - interval '20 minutes', 101)" \
  >/dev/null || { echo "not ok - fixture: setup failed"; exit 1; }
WM=$(q -c "select pgpm._from_hypertable_ctl_text(max(ts)) from v01.e_pgpm_dest")
[ -n "$WM" ] && echo "ok - fixture: copy watermark $WM" || { echo "not ok - fixture: no watermark"; exit 1; }

# A: one drain step, held open until B has finished
q -c "begin" \
  -c "select 'A-step ' || pgpm.from_hypertable_drain_appends_step('v01.e', 'ts', 1000, '$WM')" \
  -c "do \$\$ begin
        for i in 1 .. 1200 loop
          exit when exists (select 1 from pg_class where relname = 'v01_b_done');
          perform pg_sleep(0.05);
        end loop;
      end \$\$" \
  -c "commit" > /tmp/v01_a.$$ 2>&1 &
APID=$!

ok=0
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  n=$(q -c "select count(*) from pg_locks l join pg_stat_activity a on a.pid = l.pid
             where l.locktype = 'relation' and l.relation = 'v01.e_pgpm_dest'::regclass and l.mode = 'RowExclusiveLock'
               and l.granted and a.pid <> pg_backend_pid()")
  [ "$n" -ge 1 ] 2>/dev/null && { ok=1; break; }
  sleep 0.1
done
[ $ok = 1 ] && echo "ok - GUARD: drain A's step holds ROW EXCLUSIVE on the copy, its batch uncommitted" \
            || { echo "not ok - GUARD: drain A never held the copy"; wait $APID; cat /tmp/v01_a.$$; exit 1; }

# B: the documented driver, while A is in flight. It must not drain A's batch a second time (waiting for A, or
# refusing, would both be fine).
q -c "call pgpm.from_hypertable_drain_appends('v01.e', 'ts', 1000)" > /tmp/v01_b.$$ 2>&1
BRC=$?
q -c "create table public.v01_b_done ()" >/dev/null
wait $APID; ARC=$?

if [ $ARC = 0 ] && grep -q "A-step" /tmp/v01_a.$$ && ! grep -q "A-step $WM\$" /tmp/v01_a.$$; then
  echo "ok - LIVENESS: drain A copied the two appends into the copy"
else
  echo "not ok - LIVENESS: drain A copied the two appends"; cat /tmp/v01_a.$$; fail=1
fi
echo "# drain B exit $BRC: $(tr '\n' ' ' < /tmp/v01_b.$$ | cut -c1-200)"

COPY=$(q -c "select string_agg(v::text, ',' order by v) from v01.e_pgpm_dest")
if [ "$COPY" = "1,2,3,4,100,101" ]; then
  echo "ok - the copy holds each row exactly once after the two drains"
else
  echo "not ok - the copy holds each row exactly once after the two drains (have: $COPY)"; fail=1
fi
q -c "call pgpm.from_hypertable_cutover('v01.e', 'ts', interval '1 day', p_predrain => false)" > /tmp/v01_c.$$ 2>&1
echo "# cutover exit $?: $(tr '\n' ' ' < /tmp/v01_c.$$ | cut -c1-300)"
exit $fail
```

Tier 3. Found by the pass-11 fix phase's per-PR verification of PR #1196 and verified there; pre-existing on main. Related: #1167, #1135.

**Where:** `pgpm_core/install.sql:8438`

**Scenario:** transmute's orphan-child guard (_transmute_refuse_child_holders, asked in the preflight and now again after the cutover's obtain) exempts every relation that appears in pg_inherits as a child, so a relation of ANOTHER table's hierarchy (a partition of an unrelated partitioned table, an inheritance child, an index attached to a partitioned index) at a forward cell's name <rel>_p<label> is never refused; the cutover's obtain steps over the held name (_obtain_name returns null) and the conversion completes with that cell unbuilt (fail_obtain_name), every write into its range refused, where docs/reference.md lists 'a relation of any kind already holds ... a child-partition name' as refused up front. Same consequence as #1167 through the predicate the PR keeps (its body discloses it as a caveat); fails on base and head alike.

**Root cause (verifier):** transmute's orphan-child guard (_transmute_refuse_child_holders, unchanged by the PR) exempts every relation with ANY pg_inherits parent (not exists (select 1 from pg_inherits i where i.inhrelid = c.oid)), where only a partition of the table's own new parent should be exempt, so a partition of an unrelated table at a forward cell's name <rel>_p<label> is refused neither in the preflight nor in the cutover's re-asking; the cutover's obtain steps over the held name and the conversion COMPLETES with that cell unbuilt (fail_obtain_name), every write into its range failing 'no partition of relation found for row' (rebuilt by hand on head: the INSERT at hi + 36 h is refused). docs/reference.md lists 'a relation of any kind already holds ... a child-partition name' among the up-front refusals, and the code's own comment says the exemption exists for 'a partition attached to the new parent'. Tier 3 as for #1167: a documented refusal not kept, a logged write outage on one forward cell, no rows lost or silently misrouted. Reproduces on base and head (not ok 5, liveness 1-2 and guards 3-4 pass). Not known open: #1167 is the holder committed during the conversion (race), which the PR fixes; #550 is obtain's silent skip after conversion, made loud by #710's fail_obtain_name; the PR body discloses this predicate only as a caveat ('reported as an adjacent observation, not fixed here'), and no open issue names it. The finder's repro.sql is used unchanged.

**Reproduction** (`repro.sql`; fails while the defect is present, passes when absent; install: pgpm_core/install.sql):

```sql
-- V-01: transmute's orphan-child guard exempts any relation in pg_inherits, so a relation of another
-- table's hierarchy (here a partition of an unrelated table) at a forward cell's name <rel>_p<label> is not
-- refused, up front or by the cutover's new re-asking (#1167's fix keeps the predicate). The cutover's obtain
-- steps over the held name (_obtain_name returns null), and the conversion COMPLETES with that cell unbuilt:
-- a hole in the forward grid where docs/reference.md lists "a relation of any kind already holds ... a
-- child-partition name" as refused. Passes when transmute refuses or leaves no hole.
\set ON_ERROR_STOP 1
\pset format unaligned
\pset tuples_only true
create extension if not exists pgtap;
set timezone = 'UTC';
select plan(5);

create table w (id bigint not null, ts timestamptz not null, primary key (id, ts));
insert into w select i, now() - i * interval '1 minute' from generate_series(1, 60) i;

select pgpm._ts_text((date_trunc('day', now() at time zone 'UTC') + interval '1 day') at time zone 'UTC') as hi \gset
select pgpm._part_name('w', 'time', '1 day',
                       pgpm._ts_text(:'hi'::timestamptz + interval '1 day'),
                       pgpm._ts_text(:'hi'::timestamptz + interval '2 days'), 'UTC') as cell \gset

-- an unrelated partitioned table, one of whose partitions happens to carry the cell's name
create table other (k int not null, note text) partition by list (k);
select format('create table public.%I partition of other for values in (1)', :'cell') \gexec

select ok(exists (select 1 from pg_inherits where inhrelid = to_regclass(format('public.%I', :'cell'))
                    and inhparent = 'other'::regclass),
          'LIVENESS: a partition of an unrelated table holds the forward cell''s name before transmute');

-- a refusal is a pass, so the call may fail without stopping the script
\set ON_ERROR_STOP 0
call pgpm.transmute('w', 'ts', interval '1 day', p_obtain => 3);
\set ON_ERROR_STOP 1

select ok(to_regclass(format('public.%I', :'cell')) is not null,
          'LIVENESS: the holder still holds the cell''s name after the call');
select ok(not exists (select 1 from pgpm.config where parent_table = 'w'::regclass)
          or exists (select 1 from pgpm.part where parent_table = 'w'::regclass and attached
                       and lo::timestamptz = :'hi'::timestamptz),
          'GUARD: if it converted, the first forward cell [hi, hi + 1 day) was built (obtain ran in the cutover)');
select ok(not exists (select 1 from pgpm.config where parent_table = 'w'::regclass)
          or exists (select 1 from pgpm.log where parent_table = 'w'::regclass),
          'GUARD: if it converted, it logged');
select ok(not exists (select 1 from pgpm.config where parent_table = 'w'::regclass)
          or exists (select 1 from pgpm.part where parent_table = 'w'::regclass and attached
                       and lo::timestamptz <= :'hi'::timestamptz + interval '1 day'
                       and hi::timestamptz >= :'hi'::timestamptz + interval '2 days'),
          'transmute either refused or left no hole: the converted table has a partition covering [hi + 1 day, hi + 2 days)');
select * from finish();
```

Lessons from review pass 11 (pinned `0c38aae`, record `docs/reviews/2026-10-09-pass11.md`), each one mechanism, unverified beyond what the pass measured. Continues #1097 (pass 10's), #1005, #920, #849, #797, #775 and #713; the lever phase's are #1155.

1. **The fresh-surface slice outgrew one finder.** 241 ledger units (every touched unit plus one hop of callers, plus 113 touched files, the whole of docs/reference.md and CHANGELOG.md among them) against a 550k budget: the opus finder read 0.35, a re-run on its unread units 0.63, a third on the residue 0.43, for 0.86 combined; the fable duplicate read 0.39 and its re-run 0.52. Every unit of the slice was read at or above the gate by its home slice, but the slice's own gate was never met, and the pass's token cap stopped a fourth run. Split the fresh-surface slice by kind from the start (install.sql units and callers; touched tests; touched guards, scripts and documents), each with its own finder and gate, and keep the one-hop callers in the first.
2. **The per-PR mode verified the touched units and their callers, and missed a sibling copy and an upgrade state.** RC3 (Tier 1): `scripts/archive_partition_whole.sql`'s candidate query is a copy of `_archive_step`'s, which #1131 (per-PR verified) fixed for #705 without the script; a sibling copy of the mechanism is neither a touched unit nor a caller. RC4 (Tier 2): #1152's ledger backfill, verified through five rounds, attributes a chunk only under an ALWAYS block, and every release through v0.6.0 installs blocks origin-only until the first tick; the state is named in `_install_write_block`'s own #450 comment. Widen the per-PR finder's scope to every copy of the mechanism the diff touches (grep the tree for the predicate the fix adds) and to every older-install state the file's comments name for the columns the fix reads.
3. **A seed found only by the duplicate model, and a seed found only in round 2.** The pending-detach seed (S9, in `adopt_partition`) was found by the fable duplicate on the fresh-surface slice and by nobody else in fourteen other ledgers, while the opus finders on the same units read the two `inhdetachpending` clauses as present. The regrain-lock seed (S1) was noticed by three finders as a hypothesis ("the header promises the lock, the body never takes it"), built by the fable finder in round 1 and by the opus finder only in round 2 after the round-2 brief said a documented lock that is not taken is built by holding it elsewhere. A comment that promises a lock or a check is a claim to build in round 1; the finder brief should say so.
4. **Two verifiers ruled one mechanism in opposite directions.** F7-08 (fell: a wrapper may count any failure once its own LIVENESS proved the defect planted) and F7-09 (finding: the wrapper must apply discriminate.sh's premise rule) were the same defect at two wrappers; a tie-breaker ruled both findings and named a third site. When two candidates share a root cause, give them one verifier, or route the second verdict through a tie-break before grouping.
5. **A reproduction's premise failed under the harness's own flags.** F7-10's `LIVENESS:` line asserted that psql fed on stdin runs past an error; the classifier's `PSQL` carries `-v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`, so the premise failed on both trees and the claim read as invalid twice. A reproduction about how a documented command behaves must build that command itself, not through `$PSQL`; the README's reproduction contract should say what `PSQL` carries.
6. **The classifier's two readings of invalid_repro print alike.** "No `LIVENESS:` line" and "its own `LIVENESS:` line failed on the review tree" both print as `invalid_repro`; the finder added lines it already had. The summary should say which, and the sent-back note should carry the failing line.
7. **The suite check per track in parallel: the core track is the long pole.** Archive (2 seeds) and timescale (1) finished in eight minutes; the core's six seeds took seventy, one 298-file suite per seed. Run the core seeds in two halves on two containers, or plant the core seeds first and the others while the hunt runs.
8. **Three tests slices overran again** (767k, 687k, 726k against 650k) at 137, 137 and 135 files; the method's 100-file guidance stands: four tests slices next pass.
9. **Backgrounded subprocesses die with their launcher.** Three classification groups started with `&` inside one background shell were killed when it exited, and their empty logs read as "running" for a while. Launch each long job as its own background command, and check for the process, not the log.
10. **Token accounting from transcripts over-counts cached context** (usage.py summed input, output and cache reads per message: 32M for a 333k finder). Filed from the lever phase before pass 11 (2026-10-09), landing PR #1149 through the merge queue. Two observations, the first verified against the repository's settings, the second a flake candidate with the evidence so far.

1. **The Archive, TimescaleDB, Observe and eBPF tracks are not required checks, so a red one does not stop a merge group.** `main`'s branch protection requires exactly `Test Summary`, `Lint summary` and `Perf summary` (`gh api repos/neptunestation-com/pg_partition_magician/branches/main/protection/required_status_checks`); `archive.yml`, `timescale.yml`, `observe.yml`, `locktrace.yml` and `lockview.yml` have no summary job and feed none of the three. #1149's merge group (`gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-1149-d8d45bd93`, run 37965257902) had `Archive track: failure` at 17:29Z while `Test Summary`, `Lint summary` and `Perf summary` were green, and the queue merged it at 17:37Z (`ef00a6f`). `scripts/review/land.sh` waits for every check on the PR's own head (so a red archive track on the head does stop a landing), but a merge group's runs are not read by anything: a PR whose archive track goes red only in the group (an interaction with another PR of the group, or a stacked batch) lands. CLAUDE.md's "How PRs land" says the queue "merges the group only if it is green"; that is true of the three summaries only. Suggested fix: give each track a summary job (the shape `test.yml`'s `Test Summary` has: `needs` every job, `if: always()`, fails when any needed job failed or was cancelled, skips cleanly when the track's path filter skipped it) and add those summaries to the required checks; or fold the tracks into `Test Summary`. The eBPF tracks run only on Linux and skip elsewhere, which a summary that treats "skipped by filter" as green already handles.

2. **`tests/archive/db/37_parquet_snapshot_lock_entries_test.sql` assertion 6 failed once on a CI runner with `have: 5`** ("twenty uncompressed range encodes in one transaction add no lock-table entry"), in that same merge-group run, on a tree identical to #1149's head, whose own archive run (17:04Z) passed; the 24 previous merge-group archive runs were green, and three re-runs of the file against the merged tree on a local PG 17 archive container passed 6/6 each. Assertion 5 (the compressed batch, run first in the same transaction) passed in the failing run. `t37.lock_growth` counts `pg_locks` rows for the session's own pid before and after the batch, so the five extra rows were the backend's own; what they were is not in the log (the file prints `have:` only). Found in adversarial review pass pr-1102 at `42ea5b551df447ec38bcf28c4ebc4c5afd36e3a4`, root-cause group RC1: P1-03.

## P1-03

- finder: P1
- location: `pgpm_core/install.sql:9248`
- lens: fresh surface
- tier: 3
- scenario: a relation a second session is still creating at a carried index's partitioned-copy name <index>_pgpm when the cutover reaches step 9b makes its CREATE INDEX wait and die raw 23505 (pg_class_relname_nsp_index) after phases 1 and 2 committed the validated bound and the claim; both askings (preflight and under the lock) use to_regclass, which cannot see the uncommitted holder, and unlike the staging and monolith names this PR covers, the CREATE INDEX has no handler that re-asks _transmute_carried_indexes's refusal; it should refuse in pgpm's words as the up-front check does
- root cause (verifier): the carried index names <index>_pgpm are asked free only through to_regclass (_transmute_carried_indexes, in the preflight and again under the cutover's lock), which cannot see a relation another transaction is still creating, and step 9b's CREATE INDEX ... ON ONLY has no handler that re-asks that refusal after the wait, so it dies raw 23505 (pg_class_relname_nsp_index) after phases 1 and 2 committed the validated bound and the claim. Re-run with pr_classify.py: fails on base and head with every LIVENESS passing (repro.sh unchanged). Not intended: the up-front refusal ('the name(s) (...) are already taken ... Drop them, then re-run transmute') is the contract, and #1102's body only scopes carried index names out ('outside this change'). Not known open: #1105 b1 (V-03) and #1080 name the staging name, #1104 the monolith name, #766 b5 a hypertable index name length; none names the carried index copies. Tier 3 by the #1080/#1105 precedent: raw failure where pgpm promises a refusal in its words, resumable phase-2 state, no rows lost. Distinct from P1-04/V-01/V-02 (REPEATABLE READ and publications).

Reproduction: `repro.sh`, the finder's, run unchanged by the verifier.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# P1-03: #1105 bullet 1's in-flight exposure, on the carried index name <index>_pgpm, which this PR leaves
# out ("the other names the conversion creates ... are outside this change"). _transmute_carried_indexes asks
# the name free in the preflight and again under the cutover's ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, both through to_regclass,
# which cannot see a relation another transaction is still creating; step 9b's CREATE INDEX <index>_pgpm then
# waits for that transaction and dies raw with 23505 (pg_class_relname_nsp_index) once it commits, after
# phases 1 and 2 committed the validated, write-rejecting bound and the claim. The staging and monolith names
# got a handler for exactly this; this name did not. Passes when the cutover refuses in pgpm's words (the
# up-front "the name(s) (...) are already taken" refusal) or converts the table.
set -u
fail=0
out=$(mktemp); bout=$(mktemp)

$PSQL -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 >/dev/null <<'SQL'
create table public.p3 (id bigint primary key, v text not null, w int not null);
insert into public.p3 select g, 'v' || g, g % 7 from generate_series(1, 150) g;   -- step 100: monolith [0, 200)
create index p3_v_idx on public.p3 (v);
create index p3_w_idx on public.p3 (w);
create table public.p3_seen (saw boolean not null);
-- one statement, so its transaction (and the uncommitted p3_v_idx_pgpm) stays open until it returns: create
-- the name, wait until a backend holding a lock on p3 waits on this transaction, record it, return (commit)
create function public.p3_hold() returns void language plpgsql as $$
declare v_saw boolean := false;
begin
  create table public.p3_v_idx_pgpm (x int);
  for i in 1 .. 1200 loop
    v_saw := exists (select 1 from pg_locks w join pg_locks h on h.pid = w.pid
                      where w.locktype = 'transactionid' and not w.granted
                        and w.transactionid = txid_current()::text::xid
                        and h.relation = 'public.p3'::regclass and h.granted);
    exit when v_saw;
    perform pg_sleep(0.05);
  end loop;
  insert into public.p3_seen values (v_saw);
end $$;
SQL

$PSQL -q -c "set application_name = 'p1_03_holder'" -c "select public.p3_hold()" > "$bout" 2>&1 &
bpid=$!
for i in $(seq 1 100); do
  up=$($PSQL -tAc "select count(*) from pg_stat_activity where application_name = 'p1_03_holder' and wait_event = 'PgSleep'")
  [ "$up" = "1" ] && break; sleep 0.1
done
pre=$($PSQL -tAc "select to_regclass('public.p3_v_idx_pgpm') is null")
if [ "$up" = "1" ] && [ "$pre" = "t" ]; then
  echo "ok - LIVENESS: a second session is creating p3_v_idx_pgpm in a transaction still open, invisible to transmute's checks"
else
  echo "not ok - LIVENESS: the holder session never opened its window (up=$up, invisible=$pre)"; fail=1
fi

$PSQL -c "set timezone = 'UTC'" -c "call pgpm.transmute('public.p3', 'id', 100::bigint, p_obtain => 2, p_lock_timeout => '60s')" > "$out" 2>&1
wait $bpid

saw=$($PSQL -tAc "select saw from public.p3_seen")
held=$($PSQL -tAc "select relkind::text || '/' || relnatts from pg_class where oid = to_regclass('public.p3_v_idx_pgpm')")
if [ "$saw" = "t" ] && [ "$held" = "r/1" ]; then
  echo "ok - LIVENESS: the cutover, holding p3, waited on the holder's transaction, which then committed p3_v_idx_pgpm (one column, x)"
else
  echo "not ok - LIVENESS: the cutover never waited on the holder (saw=$saw, holder=$held)"; cat "$bout"; fail=1
fi
reached=$($PSQL -tAc "select (select convalidated from pg_constraint where conrelid = 'public.p3'::regclass and conname = 'pgpm_monolith_bound') and exists (select 1 from pgpm.transmute_inflight where parent_table = 'public.p3'::regclass)")
converted=$($PSQL -tAc "select count(*) from pgpm.config where parent_table = 'public.p3'::regclass")
if [ "$reached" = "t" ] || [ "$converted" = "1" ]; then
  echo "ok - LIVENESS: phases 1 and 2 committed the validated bound and the claim (or the call converted)"
else
  echo "not ok - LIVENESS: transmute never reached its cutover: $(grep -m1 ERROR "$out")"; fail=1
fi
echo "ok - GUARD: the call ended with: $(grep -m1 ERROR "$out" || echo '(no error)')"
if [ "$converted" = "1" ]; then
  echo "ok - the cutover carried the conversion through"
elif grep -q "ERROR:  pg_partition_magician:.*p3_v_idx_pgpm" "$out"; then
  echo "ok - the cutover refused the held index name in pgpm's words"
else
  echo "not ok - the cutover died raw after phases 1 and 2 committed the bound and the claim: $(grep -m1 ERROR "$out")"; fail=1
fi
rm -f "$out" "$bout"
exit $fail
```

Method and harness lessons from the pass-9 fix phase (record: docs/reviews/2026-10-06-pass9.md, fix-phase section), the counterpart of #1005 (the pass's review lessons) and #964 (pass 8's). Each is a change to a brief, a script or a document, not a defect in pgpm; none needs a verifier.

- [ ] **A stricter certification rule lands last and is re-run on the final tree.** #1029 (discriminate refuses a liveness-only mutant run) passed its own full discriminate run on the tree it was cut from and failed on the rebased tree: two other fixes of the same phase (#1022, #1012) changed what `archive_object_key_digits_only`'s symptom is (the collision is refused, not overwritten), tests/archive/db/16 aborted after 8 of 23 and its only `not ok` was a liveness line. The remedy was to assert the contract (the stem's shape) before the fixture that can abort. Write into `/fix-phase`: a rule-tightening PR is spawned with the wave but landed last, and its fixer re-runs the track on the rebased head before the coordinator enqueues it.
- [ ] **Three fixers extending one guard script is one hand merge, not three.** G17, G18 and G19 appended under their own comment at the end of `bench/tests_fail_on_defect.sh` as briefed, and those hunks merged as add/add; the dispatch near the top, which each also had to touch, stopped the batch (#1019). Next time the brief assigns the dispatch's extension to one fixer, or the guard gains a per-group include file.
- [ ] **The Archive track is not a required queue check.** pr-1007's merge group failed the Archive track (tests/archive/db/37 assertion 6, a lock-count variance) and merged anyway because the three required summaries (Test, Lint, Perf) were green. Whether the archive and timescale tracks should feed a required summary is a ruleset decision for the maintainer.
- [ ] **The bitnami MinIO image needs `--entrypoint minio ... server /bitnami/minio/data --address :9000`.** The pass-8 brief recipe (image entrypoint kept, `server /data`) exits with "file access denied"; three archive fixers worked around it before the brief was patched. The fixer brief template and `scripts/review/README.md` should carry the compose service's exact command.
- [ ] **`gate.sh` is not FIFO and fourteen fixers queue for over an hour behind four-minute runs** (waits of 70 to 78 minutes measured). A per-fixer compose project name (`docker compose -p pgpm_fix_G7`) would remove the serialisation; failing that, the brief should tell fixers to run the gated suite once and keep working on proofs while they wait.
- [ ] **GitHub closes an issue on `Fixes #N bullet 3`.** The closing-keyword parser ignores the qualifier, so #713 and #766 were closed by their partial fixes and had to be reopened. The fixer brief should say `Addresses #N (bullet 3)` for a partial fix and reserve `Fixes`/`Closes` for a whole issue.
- [ ] **Fixers' interim "completed" notices while a gated run is pending** (nine of 23 in this phase) read as reports; the coordinator must wait for the hand-back. The brief now says to run the gated suite in the foreground; the harness could also mark a hand-back distinctly.
- [ ] **Reproductions that cannot pass under any correct fix** (F9-08 writes immediately after a GRANT with no tick between; F13-07 expects a hand-over no role can perform; F5-05 dies unguarded at the refusal the issue itself asked for): the verifier's acceptance step should ask "which correct behaviours would this reproduction accept?", and a reproduction that accepts only one of the issue's stated remedies should say so.
- [ ] **Landing measured**: 23 PRs in 18.2 h wall-clock (the per-PR durations sum to 43.4 h, which `landing_stats.py` prints as its total and the first record draft misread as wall-clock), median 32 minutes from enqueue to merge and 108 from a PR's landing turn to its merge because the queue builds the stacked groups one at a time (a batch's fifth PR waits for four merge groups), two hand stops, one real CI failure (the rule interaction above), no retried flakes, 42 file resolutions by `keep_both.py`, one 45-minute merge-group starvation behind the fixers' head runs on the first landing. Lessons from review pass 9 (pinned `06643c8`, record `docs/reviews/2026-10-06-pass9.md`), each one mechanism, unverified beyond what the pass measured. Continues #920 (pass 8's), #849, #797, #775 and #713.

1. **Catalogue mutations carry `-- MUTANT` markers in their replacement text, which makes them loud seeds.** Two of this pass's three catalogue seeds (`archive_object_key_search_path_parent`, `obtain_backoff_bypass_shifts_cell`) left a literal `-- MUTANT` comment beside the planted line, and four finders (F4, F5, F6, F9) said so in their claims ("the line carries a stray `-- MUTANT (#913)` comment, so this is probably a planted seed"). `plant_seeds.py` should strip `-- MUTANT...` comments from a mutation's replacement text when it plants (the catalogue's markers are for `discriminate.sh`, not for a review tree), and the planting rule should say that a catalogue seed is read for its markers before it is sealed.
2. **A catalogue mutation's anchor can drift into removing far more than its defect.** `untransmute_no_recheck_under_lock` (S7) is documented as removing "the lock-and-recheck block only"; on this tree its regex removes untransmute's whole lock-and-capture block, so the restored table lost row-level security, its policies, grants and publications, and an identity-column table could not be untransmuted at all. Twenty pgTAP files caught it, three finders filed its consequences as Tier 1 (F1-01, F1-02, F9-06, F13-01, F13-02) and the classifier could not place three of them. The mutation must be re-anchored (the capture block moved under the lock in #767's fix, after the mutation was written), and `bench/untransmute_race.sh` still reports discrimination against it only because the mutant breaks much more than the race. A `--selftest`-shaped check that a mutation's edit touches no more lines than its description names would catch this class.
3. **A novel seed's consequence must be demonstrated on the seeded tree before it is sealed.** S4 (the anchor half of `_id_step_contract` dropped) was sealed as Tier 2 on the reading that an off-granularity anchor would commit a bound the cutover's ATTACH rounds; on the tree, `_control_bound_contract` refuses that bound before anything commits, so the seed's whole consequence is a wrong remedy in the refusal message. Two finders (F1, F10) read the site, wrote the hypothesis and judged it not worth a claim for exactly that reason, and it reads as a missed seed. The sealed record should carry a coordinator-run reproduction per novel seed, run against the seeded tree (fails) and the pristine one (passes), as a claim must: `plant_seeds.py --prove`.
4. **The suite check's output is block-buffered until the process exits.** `plant_seeds.py --suite` under `nohup ... > suite.log` wrote nothing for 2.5 hours; progress was readable only from the harness's database names (`pgpm_seed_s9_191`). Run it under `python3 -u` or flush after each row, and print the per-seed row when the seed's run ends.
5. **Verifiers that find a seed-reached claim should store the rebuilt reproduction that passes on pristine.** F9-02 and F12-02 reached their defects only on the review tree (the hand-over and the hypertable-schema seeds); both verifiers returned `fell` with no rebuild ("no rebuild can reach a defect the pristine code does not contain"), so the classifier could not record the hits until asked for a reproduction whose LIVENESS lines assert only the premises. `verifier.md` step 4 should say that a claim absent from the pristine commit is a seed hit when a reproduction passes there and fails on the review tree, and that writing that reproduction is the verifier's last act for it.
6. **Reproductions that create cluster-wide roles collide between the two trees' runs.** F13-06 and F13-07 failed on the pristine run with "role ... already exists" because the review-tree run had created the role in the same cluster; both verifiers rebuilt with `if not exists`. The reproduction contract should say that roles are created only when missing and dropped at the end, and the classifier could drop roles named `<finder>_*` between its runs.
7. **The tests slice B is too large for one finder.** F11 spent 893k tokens against a 550k guide to read 180 files ("the slice is about 1.4 MB"), the second pass running; F10 (167 files) read 74 and needed a re-run. Three tests slices next pass, or two plus the archive and timescale tests as their own.
8. **The carried bench sum-only seed was found on the fourth attempt, through the round-2 rule.** The brief's "build every pre-pass line marked claimed before anything else" and the round-2 brief's precedence rule turned the fourth finder's pre-pass line into F7-01 in round 1. Keep both sentences in the brief; the blind spot was the budget rule, not the reading.
9. **The coordinator never rendered F8's round-2 brief**, and the finder worked from the message text instead (same rules, same outcome). Render every round-2 brief at hunt start, not per report.
10. **The novel seeds of passes 6 to 9 are still uncatalogued** (#920 item 9): this pass's five novel patches are in the pass directory's `seeds/` with their `edits.json`; S3 (the enumeration without the hypertable delta) and S2 (the schema check dropped) are siblings of findings filed this pass, and belong in `bench/mutations/mutate.py` with the guard that catches them.

The seed was withdrawn and replaced by a novel one; the eight measured results were carried into the new sealed record by hand, which `--suite --only` should do itself when the plan changes.
2. **`coverage.py` lower-cases the ledger's unit names but not a files slice's paths**, so `README.md`, `RELEASING.md`, `ONBOARDING.md` and `pgpm_archive/README.md` can never match: F6's files part read 0.64 in the tool and 11 of 11 in its ledger. Compare case-insensitively on both sides (SQL identifiers are already folded).

A hypothesis that names a count-for-identity shape should not be the finder's to leave: either the coordinator builds the pre-pass's "claimed / pinned / not-identity" verdicts into claims mechanically for the two cardinality shapes, or round 2's brief says that every pre-pass line marked WEAK is built before anything else.

Lessons from review pass 7 (pinned `4060f6b`, record `docs/reviews/2026-10-02-pass7.md`), each one mechanism, unverified beyond what the pass measured. Continues #797 (pass 6's), #775 (pass 5's) and #713 (pass 4's).

1. **The four carried seeds were missed a second time, and this time nobody noticed them at all.** Pass 6's four missed novel seeds were re-planted verbatim (a bench identity assertion weakened to `sum(n)`, a pgTAP identity assertion weakened to `count(*)` under a header promising asymmetric fixtures, a janitor's per-child isolation removed, the regrain analyse block in its pre-repair shape). In pass 6 three of them were in finders' hypotheses; in pass 7 none was: two were not reached (both bench finders spent their budgets on the hypertable wrappers and the verdict machinery and neither null-results file mentions `bench/cutover_trigger_window.sh`; `tests/194` was read "in part"), two were read and judged sound (`_enforce_regrain_capture` "takes try-lock, then reads config: held"; "The ANALYZE of the delta on reltuples < 0 happens once per run (#710). Held.", where the seed's reverted comment supplies the #710 reasoning and the reader trusted it). A blind spot stable across two passes and two finder populations is a property of the method, not of a finder. For the two cardinality shapes the honest tool is mechanical: a pre-pass that lists every `count(*)`, `sum(`, length and `grep -c` assertion in `bench/` and `tests/` whose description, header or neighbouring comment names rows, triggers or identity, for a finder (or the coordinator) to read one by one. For the two reading shapes there is no mechanical form; a seed that carries its own justification in a comment is read as correct, which argues for the lens text to say "read the code against its comment, not the comment".
2. **Round 2 (hand each finder its hypotheses back) is cheap and productive, and does not repair a blind spot.** 24 claims for 128k finder tokens and 24 verifier runs (about 1.05M in all): 14 findings, 3 of them Tier 1, 8 re-finds of open issues, 2 of the pass's 3 fallen claims, 0 seeds. Cost per finding about half of round 1's. It belongs in the skill as a standing step, with its results reported separately (its precision 0.58 strict / 0.92 counting re-finds against round 1's 0.67 / 0.98). But it only builds what a finder already wrote down, so it cannot find a seed no finder noticed.
3. **Strict precision fell below the criteria's 0.7 (0.64) because of the known-open backlog, not reaching.** 23 of the 69 claims re-found nine open issues, 19 of them for the first time with a built reproduction; eight of the nine issues are the fixers' adjacent-observation lists filed unverified one to three days before the pass (#813 to #819, #766 to #775), which finders cannot see. Only 3 claims fell. The definition `(findings + seed hits) / claims` counts a reproduced, open defect as a false report; it measures the size of the unverified backlog, not whether finders reached. Either the definition should count a verified known-open re-find as a true report (and report the strict figure beside it), or the backlog issues should be verified or closed before the next pass is pinned, or both. Pass 6 already reported "1.00 counting re-finds"; this pass reports 0.97.
4. **A claim that bundles a seed with a real defect loses the seed's attribution.** F7-03 and F10-02 each tested SET NOT NULL (seed S7) and ADD CHECK (#817, open) in one reproduction; both failed on the pristine commit too, classified as candidates, and the verifiers dropped the seeded half. Recall was unaffected (S7 was hit by two other finders) but a seed found by one finder alone in that shape would read as missed. `classify_claims.py` could flag a candidate whose review-tree failure set is a strict superset of its pristine failure set ("part of this reproduction fails only on the review tree") for the verifier to split.
5. **A seed claim whose pristine assertion is unsound reads as a candidate until a verifier rebuilds it.** F10-01 (seed S9) compared `untransmute(...)` with `'app.events'::regclass::oid` in the same statement; the constant is bound at planning time, before the function runs, so the pristine run failed for a reason that was not the defect. The verifier's rebuilt reproduction passes on the pristine commit, the final classification (which prefers `repro.verified.sql`) records the hit, and the "fell" verdict is kept aside. Two tooling consequences: the coordinator must re-run the full classification after verification (the skill's step 7 reads the pre-verification file), and `pass_metrics.py` should ignore a verdict for a claim the classification no longer calls a candidate rather than counting it.
6. **The classifier's exact `LIVENESS:` prefix rule bit once.** F3-02 labelled its premise checks `LIVENESS A:` / `LIVENESS B:` and was rejected as `invalid_repro` without running; fixed in round 2. finder.md should give the two-label form (`LIVENESS: (A) ...`).
7. **The fleet image segfaults on `grant ... to current_user`.** At 11:13:18Z a finder's statement crashed a backend in `pgpm_test-timescale` (public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgres:15.14.1.127) and the postmaster restarted every backend; the finder avoided it afterwards and the verifier briefs carried a warning. #816 already records two fleet-image faults; this is a third, and the skill's harness notes should name it.
8. **The archive harness still comes up without its bucket** (#797 item 1 is open): the coordinator created it by hand before the suite check and the controls were clean first time. And pass 6's nine novel seeds were not added to `bench/mutations/mutate.py` by its fix phase (the methodology's "fixed defects become seeds" step); this pass's four novel seeds and the four carried ones are in the pass directory's `seeds/` and should be catalogued together.

Scratch for every number: the pass directory named in the record's coordinator notes (`sealed.json`, `suite.log`, `classified.json`, `verdicts.json`, `tokens_harness.tsv`, `verifiers_tokens.tsv`, `per_finder.tsv`, the ten `null-results.md`, `round1_claims.txt`, `round2_claims.txt`).
title: pass-7 method lessons: the four carried seeds missed again (two unreached, two read as sound), round 2 is cheap and does not repair a blind spot, strict precision measures the known-open backlog, a seed bundled with a real defect or behind an unsound assertion loses its attribution, the exact LIVENESS: prefix, a fleet-image segfault

Lessons from review pass 6 (pinned `ae5dddc`, record `docs/reviews/2026-10-01-pass6.md`), each one mechanism, unverified beyond what the pass measured. Continues #775 (pass 5's) and #713 (pass 4's).

1. **The archive harness is not up when `docker compose --profile archive up -d` returns.** MinIO starts, but the test bucket (`archive-test-bucket`) is created by `test.sh`'s `run_archive` and by `closure.sh` with a SigV4 PUT through `curlimages/curl` on the compose network. The review-pass skill's harness step (`.claude/skills/review-pass/SKILL.md`, step 4) says only "Start `pgpm_test-15`" and the finder brief tells the archive finder the bucket exists. In pass 6 the coordinator brought the three profiles up and the first suite check's archive control failed 19 of 27 files with no seed planted; every file that touches MinIO failed, the eight that do not passed. Fix: the skill names the bucket step (or `plant_seeds.py --suite` and the coordinator's bring-up share closure.sh's readiness and bucket block).
2. **`plant_seeds.py --suite` accepted a control that failed 19 of 27 files and measured a seed against it.** It sealed the failures as `suite_noise` and reported S5 "not caught; noise ..." for a seed the re-run (`--only S5 --rebaseline`, after the bucket existed) showed `tests/archive/db/26` catches. Its own docstring calls the control the runner's liveness witness. A control that fails more than a file or two is a broken harness, not noise: the check should refuse to seal it (exit non-zero, name the failing files) unless told the noise is expected.
3. **Three of the four missed seeds were seen by a finder and written up as hypotheses, not claims.** S1 (the regrain analyse block in its pre-repair shape) is F8's hypothesis almost verbatim; S8 (the janitor's per-child isolation removed) is F4's hypothesis, describing the consequence of the missing isolation without noticing the isolation is missing; S3 (a bench assertion weakened to a sum) is F9's hypothesis, argued down as unexploitable in context. The methodology makes a hypothesis free and a weak claim costly, which is right, and under a budget that real defects were consuming (every finder's upheld findings) the seed-shaped observation lost. Recall 0.56 (read-caught 0.43) is the first below the criteria's 0.8. **Status: unverified candidates**, left out of #496's fix (PR #532) by its fixer and recorded here so they are not lost.

1. `_regrain_capture_names` now resolves the delta table and trigger function by identity (#496), returning `nsp`, `delta`, `fn`. But `_regrain_reconcile`, the purge, the swap and `regrain_cancel` still format the delta relation as `%I.%I` from the PARENT's current schema plus the resolved delta name, not from the resolver's `nsp`. 2. A regrain begun BEFORE the #496 upgrade, whose parent was renamed mid-run, has a delta table under the old derived name that the new resolver no longer maps to. The run itself is recoverable (`regrain_restart`), but the legacy delta table and its trigger function stay behind, a leak with no data risk. `uninstall.sql` removes only what `_regrain_capture_names` can name.

- Use the resolver's `nsp` in all four callers (a one-line change each) and add a mutation that puts the parent-schema derivation back in one of them, caught by the existing `bench/regrain_capture_identity.sh` extended with a schema move under a relaxed guard, or simply by a unit test of the derivation.
- For item 2, a one-time sweep at install (like #498's `dropped_fk` backfill) that finds `*_pgpm_regrain_delta` relations with no owning `pgpm.config` row and logs or drops them.
title: regrain change capture: reconcile, purge, swap and cancel pair the delta NAME with the parent's schema, not the resolver's, and a pre-upgrade run whose parent was renamed keeps an orphan legacy delta

**Status: unverified candidates**, three related observations from the fixers of #511 (PR #540) and #518/#519 (PRs #546/#547). Filed together because they share a mechanism: archive candidate selection and ledger hygiene do not know about the regrain lifecycle.

1. **A source is archived during its own regrain, and the swap discards that coverage.** `_archive_step` picks candidates by eligibility and coverage; nothing excludes the child that `regrain_cursor` is currently copying. Each tick can export a chunk of the source that the swap will then reset (`archive_coverage_reset`, #518). The export is wasted work and wasted bucket space, and on a compressed budget it can be minutes per tick. Proposed: exclude the `regrain_cursor` child from archive candidates while a run is in flight (the fine children archive from their own `lo` after the swap).
2. **Partial-chunk objects stay unreferenced in the bucket.** When coverage is reset (#518) or a chunk is discarded, the objects those ledger rows pointed at are left in the store with nothing referencing them. Not a correctness issue (nothing is lost), but an operator has no way to find or reap them. Proposed: log the discarded keys in the `archive_coverage_reset` row (or a companion row) so a reaper can act on them.
3. **`retire()` and `untransmute()` leave `pgpm.archive_ledger` rows keyed by a dropped partition or parent.** The reference documents that rows stay. Worth deciding whether that is the contract (then say why: the ledger is the audit trail of what was exported) or a leak (then sweep on drop). The fixer of #517 noted the untransmute case; the fixer of #511 the retire case.

## Suggested acceptance

- Item 1: `bench/` guard that runs a regrain with archiving on and asserts no `archive_chunk` log row names the cursor child between `regrain_prepare` and the swap, with a liveness witness that other children DID archive in the same window; mutation removes the exclusion.
- Item 2 and 3 are chores unless a decision turns them into contracts; they need a doc change either way.
title: archive coverage and the regrain lifecycle: a source keeps being archived during its own regrain, partial-chunk objects go unreferenced, and dropped partitions keep ledger rows
